source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.campus_sqft_context: CyrusOne's centrally located CIN2 data center campus provides colocation, backup and recovery. Located near downtown Cincinnati, OH, CyrusOne's CIN2 data center is conveniently located 15 minutes from Greater Cincinnati and the Northern Kentucky International airports. As Cincinnati's primary carrier hotel facility, CIN2 offers 143,778 sq. ft. of IT technical space and is High-Performance Computing (HPC) capable. The center's design includes closed loop chilled water cooling with redundant feeds for makeup water, comprehensive security measures, and is on FEMA's priority list. The facility provides production colocation, backup and recovery, and business continuity solutions with proven reliability.

reading.body:
CyrusOne CIN2 sits on 143,778 square feet of IT technical space in downtown Cincinnati and publishes 11 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 11 MW supports roughly 275 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it supports roughly 1,100 racks. The operator describes the facility as HPC-capable and uses closed-loop chilled water cooling, which is a prerequisite for sustained high-density compute loads, but the published figure of 11 MW places a hard ceiling on how much of that capability can be exercised at once.

The four certifications frame what workloads this campus can legally host. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data processing. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 qualifies it for workloads requiring a certified information-security management system. FISMA qualifies it for certain federal government workloads. Together they make the campus eligible for regulated-industry AI inference and data pipelines, though which tenants are actually present is not published.

Within Ohio, this site holds meaningful weight. Of 76 data center facilities mapped in the state, only five publish a megawatt figure, and those five sum to 38.6 MW. CIN2's 11 MW ranks second among that group, representing roughly 28 percent of all published Ohio capacity on this site. That share reflects the limits of disclosure as much as the limits of the state's infrastructure, because most mapped facilities publish no capacity figure at all. For an AI workload requiring regulated compliance and proximity to Midwest network interconnects, CIN2 is a credible candidate, though its 11 MW ceiling means it is better suited to inference or analytics at moderate scale than to large-scale model training.
